item.content:encoded:
Bienvenue dans la première session du Sommet Virtuel organisé par Alegria Group : une masterclass intensive dédiée à l’implémentation concrète des super-agents IA et de l’écosystème No-Code pour transformer sa productivité et bâtir un avantage concurrentiel décisif.

🇫🇷 Version Française

Synthèse & Points Clés à Retenir

Dans cette première soirée du sommet, Francis et l’équipe d’Alegria Group exposent la rupture technologique actuelle : le passage de la simple utilisation de prompts textuels (ChatGPT, Claude) à l’orchestration de systèmes autonomes et de super-agents IA interconnectés.

  • Le piège du simple “chat” : Moins de 1% des utilisateurs exploitent l’IA au-delà d’une interface de messagerie basique.
  • L’effet de levier des agents No-Code : Connecter des modèles de langage (LLMs) à des outils métier (CRM, facturation, emails, bases de données) permet de créer des systèmes qui tournent sans intervention humaine continue.
  • Monétisation de la valeur : Se concentrer sur des problèmes coûteux et chronophages chez les clients ou dans son organisation pour générer un retour sur investissement immédiat.

Découpage Horodaté de la Session

  • [00:00] - Accueil de la communauté internationale et cadrage des 5 jours du Sommet.
  • [15:30] - Pourquoi 99% des gens utilisent mal l’IA et restent bloqués au stade de débutant.
  • [32:10] - Les piliers d’un Super-Agent IA : Perception, Raisonnement, Action et Mémoire.
  • [54:45] - Cartographie des cas d’usage à fort ROI (automatisation de devis, facturation, support client).
  • [01:18:20] - Architecture type : Relier un LLM à des connecteurs No-Code (Make, n8n, Airtable).
  • [01:42:00] - Session interactive de questions-réponses et plan d’action pour le Jour 2.

Analyse Technique Approfondie : Du Prompt à l’Agent Autonome

Pour véritablement surpasser la majorité des utilisateurs, il convient d’adopter l’architecture des Agents Autonomes :

Composant Rôle Technique Outils Recommandés
Cerveau (Reasoning Engine) Analyse, prise de décision et synthèse Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o
Orchestrateur (Workflow) Routage logique et déclencheurs n8n, Make, Zapier
Mémoire & Contexte (Vector DB / DB) Stockage structuré des informations métier Airtable, Supabase, Pinecone
Exécuteurs d’Actions (Tools) Envoi d’emails, génération de PDF, webhooks Stripe, Gmail API, Slack

Exemple de Script de Déclenchement d’un Agent (n8n / Node.js)

import axios from 'axios';

interface AgentPayload {
  leadEmail: string;
  inquiryText: string;
  urgencyScore: number;
}

async function dispatchAIAgent(payload: AgentPayload): Promise<void> {
  const webhookUrl = 'https://n8n.instance.internal/webhook/ai-agent-triage';
  
  const response = await axios.post(webhookUrl, {
    email: payload.leadEmail,
    query: payload.inquiryText,
    score: payload.urgencyScore,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
  });

  console.log(`[Agent Triggered] Status: ${response.status} - ID: ${response.data.executionId}`);
}

Citations Marquantes & Philosophie

“L’IA ne va pas remplacer les humains, mais les professionnels qui maîtrisent l’orchestration des agents IA remplaceront tous ceux qui l’ignorent.” — Francis, Alegria Group

Conclusion & Ressources

Ce premier jour pose les fondations indispensables pour construire une activité scalable et pérenne grâce à l’intelligence artificielle. Pensez à formaliser vos processus répétitifs avant de les automatiser.

🇬🇧 English Version

Executive Summary & Key Takeaways

In this kickoff session of the Virtual Summit, Alegria Group breaks down the modern AI landscape: shifting from isolated chat prompts to autonomous AI super-agents backed by No-Code architectures.

  • Beyond the Chatbot : Over 99% of people remain trapped in simple conversational prompts without building automated backend value.
  • No-Code Compounding Effect: Integrating LLMs directly into transactional business pipelines (CRMs, invoicing, inbound support) unlocks 24/7 automated operations.
  • High-Value Problem Selection: Focus AI deployment on mission-critical, expensive bottlenecks to achieve immediate ROI.

  • [00:00] - Welcome, global audience check-in, and 5-day summit overview.
  • [15:30] - The fundamental mistake 99% of users make with generative AI.
  • [32:10] - Anatomy of an AI Super-Agent: Perception, Logic, Action, and Memory.
  • [54:45] - Identifying high-leverage business processes for rapid automation.
  • [01:18:20] - Technical blueprint: Combining LLMs with No-Code platforms (Make, n8n, Airtable).
  • [01:42:00] - Live community Q&A and preview of Day 2.

Deep Technical Dive: Agent Architecture

Transitioning from manual prompting to production-grade agents requires modular infrastructure:

Layer Functionality Recommended Stack
Reasoning Engine Deep semantic understanding and decision logic Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o
Workflow Orchestration Event-driven execution and branching n8n, Make, Zapier
State & Memory Structured data persistence and vector context Airtable, Supabase, Pinecone
Action Endpoints Transactional APIs, notifications, doc generation Stripe, Resend, Slack Webhooks

Example Automation Webhook Dispatcher

import axios from 'axios';

interface AgentPayload {
  leadEmail: string;
  inquiryText: string;
  urgencyScore: number;
}

async function dispatchAIAgent(payload: AgentPayload): Promise<void> {
  const webhookUrl = 'https://n8n.instance.internal/webhook/ai-agent-triage';
  
  const response = await axios.post(webhookUrl, {
    email: payload.leadEmail,
    query: payload.inquiryText,
    score: payload.urgencyScore,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString()

  console.log(`[Agent Triggered] Status: ${response.status} - ID: ${response.data.executionId}`);

Key Takeaway Quote

“AI won’t directly replace humans, but operators orchestrating autonomous agents will rapidly displace everyone stuck in legacy workflows.” — Francis, Alegria Group

Conclusion

Mastering agentic workflows is the ultimate competitive moat for modern professionals and tech entrepreneurs. Map your bottlenecks today and prepare for system execution in the upcoming sessions.

item.title: Docker Rebuilt Itself for AI Agents – What Went Right and What Went Wrong
item.author: brzulovic@gmail.com
item.description: Docker has quietly spent the last year re‑architecting its platform to serve the exploding market of AI agents. From a native Model Runner that treats LLMs as OCI artifacts, to a Micro‑Container Proxy (MCP) gateway, micro‑VM sandboxes, and a library of hardened distroless images, Docker is positioning itself as the “Docker for AI”. Cloud Codes walks through each launch, highlights the engineering trade‑offs, and points out a critical security misstep that could erode developer trust.
item.content:encoded:
Docker has quietly spent the last year re‑architecting its platform to serve the exploding market of AI agents. From a native Model Runner that treats LLMs as OCI artifacts, to a Micro‑Container Proxy (MCP) gateway, micro‑VM sandboxes, and a library of hardened distroless images, Docker is positioning itself as the “Docker for AI”. Cloud Codes walks through each launch, highlights the engineering trade‑offs, and points out a critical security misstep that could erode developer trust.

Executive Summary & Key Takeaways

  • Docker’s AI stack consists of four major components: Model Runner, MCP gateway, sbx micro‑VM sandboxes, and 1,000+ hardened images.
  • Model Runner integrates with Docker Compose via a models block, allowing LLMs to be versioned and deployed like any container.
  • The MCP gateway introduced a powerful tool‑gateway pattern but suffered a CVSS‑10 vulnerability (Ruflo) that allowed unauthenticated shell execution.
  • Docker’s custom VMM replaces Firecracker on macOS/Windows, solving cross‑platform limitations but adding maintenance overhead.
  • While Docker’s offering is technically impressive, community adoption still favors Ollama due to simplicity, star count, and a more mature ecosystem.
  • The price‑increase controversy and the security scandal have created a trust deficit that Docker must address to win back developers.

Timestamped Chapter Breakdown / Key Moments

Timestamp Topic
00:00 Docker’s Quiet AI Transformation
00:23 Launch #1 – Docker Model Runner (docker model run)
02:22 Native Docker Compose Integration (models block)
03:11 Ollama vs Docker – why Solomon Hykes backs Ollama
03:37 Launch #2 – MCP Gateway & Ruflo CVSS 10.0 scandal
05:54 Launch #3 – sbx MicroVM Sandboxes & YOLO mode
07:08 Why Firecracker failed on macOS/Windows – Docker’s custom VMM
08:00 Launch #4 – 1,000+ Hardened Distroless Images (free)
08:46 Price increase controversy & trust deficit
09:27 Final Verdict – What to use vs what to skip

Detailed Topic Deep‑Dive

1. Docker Model Runner

Docker Model Runner treats an LLM as an OCI image under the docker.io/ai namespace. The command syntax mirrors standard container execution:

# Pull a model OCI artifact
docker pull docker.io/ai/llama-2:7b

# Run the model locally
docker model run llama-2:7b --port 8080

The models block in a docker-compose.yml file enables multi‑model orchestration:

services:
  agent:
    image: my/agent:latest
    models:
      - name: llama-2
        image: docker.io/ai/llama-2:7b
      - name: embedding
        image: docker.io/ai/text-embedding:3.0

This design gives developers the same declarative workflow they already use for containers, simplifying version control, CI/CD, and scaling.

2. MCP Gateway & Ruflo Vulnerability

The Micro‑Container Proxy (MCP) acts as a side‑car that forwards API calls from an agent to external services. Docker released a tool‑gateway pattern that abstracts credential handling and request routing.

# Start the MCP server (default namespace: ruflo)
docker mcp start --namespace ruflo

Unfortunately, the initial release exposed the MCP HTTP endpoint without authentication. The Ruflo CVSS 10.0 vulnerability allowed any unauthenticated caller to execute arbitrary shell commands on the host, a severe breach of the isolation model.

Docker patched the issue within days, but the incident highlighted the risk of exposing internal gateways without proper auth layers.

3. sbx MicroVM Sandboxes & YOLO Mode

Docker’s sbx CLI launches a lightweight micro‑VM sandbox using a custom VMM that works across Apple Hypervisor, Windows Hypervisor Platform, and KVM. It replaces the soft permission prompts of traditional containers with hard kernel boundaries.

# Run Claude in a sandbox (YOLO mode skips interactive prompts)
docker sbx run claude --yolo

The custom VMM was built because Firecracker does not support macOS/Windows natively. By writing their own monitor, Docker achieved cross‑platform parity but introduced a new code‑base to maintain.

4. Hardened Distroless Images

Docker open‑sourced 1,000+ hardened distroless images that strip unnecessary binaries, reduce attack surface, and are signed with Notary v2. They are free to pull from Docker Hub, providing a secure baseline for AI workloads.

# Example of a hardened image for a Python inference service
docker pull docker.io/ai/hardened-python:3.11-slim

These images complement the Model Runner approach, ensuring that even custom model containers start from a minimal, vetted base.

Code Snippets & Examples

# Full workflow: pull model, start MCP, run sandbox, expose via Compose
docker pull docker.io/ai/llama-2:7b

docker mcp start --namespace ruflo &

docker sbx run llama-2 --yolo --port 8080 &

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  ai-agent:
    image: my/agent:latest
    depends_on:
      - mcp
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      MCP_ENDPOINT: http://mcp:5000
  mcp:
    image: docker.io/ai/mcp:latest
    command: start --namespace ruflo

Key Quotes & Speaker Insights

  • “Docker’s Model Runner is a game‑changer for reproducible AI, but you still need to trust the supply chain.” – Cloud Codes
  • “The Ruflo incident shows that convenience can’t trump security; a gateway without auth is a backdoor waiting to be exploited.” – Cloud Codes
  • “Ollama’s simplicity and massive star count keep it ahead in community adoption, despite Docker’s richer feature set.” – Cloud Codes

Conclusion & Related Resources

Docker’s AI stack is technically sophisticated and brings container‑native ergonomics to LLM deployment. However, the security misstep with MCP and the price‑increase backlash have created a trust gap. For teams that prioritize reproducibility and cross‑platform sandboxing, Docker’s offering is compelling; for rapid prototyping and community support, Ollama remains the go‑to solution.

Further Reading

  • Docker Model Runner Docs: https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner/
  • Docker Sandbox Repository: https://github.com/docker/sandbox
  • Ollama GitHub: https://github.com/ollama/ollama
  • Wiz MCP Security Audit: https://www.wiz.io/blog
  • Ruflo Agent Framework: https://github.com/ruflo-ai/ruflo

Stay tuned for more deep‑dives into emerging infrastructure patterns.

item.title: Diagram-Design: AI-Powered Technical Diagrams Styled to Your Brand
item.author: brzulovic@gmail.com
item.description:
Creating clean, visually appealing technical architecture diagrams is often a tedious task. Whether you are constantly tweaking coordinates in Excalidraw or wrestling with the default layout quirks of Mermaid, producing polished graphics for documentation and presentations takes time.

Enter Diagram-design, an open-source skill built for AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. It automates the generation of publication-ready, standalone HTML diagrams without requiring complex build steps or external image dependencies.
item.content:encoded:
Creating clean, visually appealing technical architecture diagrams is often a tedious task. Whether you are constantly tweaking coordinates in Excalidraw or wrestling with the default layout quirks of Mermaid, producing polished graphics for documentation and presentations takes time.

Enter Diagram-design, an open-source skill built for AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. It automates the generation of publication-ready, standalone HTML diagrams without requiring complex build steps or external image dependencies.

Standalone HTML Diagrams with Zero Build Friction

Diagram-design outputs standalone HTML files that you can open directly in any browser. It supports 27 distinct diagram types, including:

  • System architecture schematics
  • Sequence diagrams
  • Finite state machines
  • Gantt project timelines
  • Quadrant and matrix charts

Each diagram is available out of the box in three aesthetic themes: Light, Dark, and Editorial.

Smart Redrawing: Beyond Simple Format Conversion

Instead of acting as a naive format converter, Diagram-design acts as an automated graphic designer. You can feed it existing files, such as a .drawio file, an embedded .drawio.png, or raw Mermaid syntax embedded in a README.md.

What it discards:

  • Absolute layout coordinates and manual canvas placement
  • Outdated fonts and custom palette overrides
  • Diagonal connector clutter and awkward auto-alignments

What it preserves:

  • Core components and functional nodes
  • Relationship hierarchies and logic flows
  • Groupings, subgraphs, and natural reading order

At the end of the import, Diagram-design outputs a fidelity report detailing input nodes, rendered entities, and any orphaned elements removed during cleanup.

Four Axes of Customization

Diagram-design adapts the generated output across four distinct dimensions depending on your target medium and audience:

Axis Configuration Options Description
Format HTML, SVG, PNG Clean standalone vector HTML/SVG or pixel-perfect PNG (rendered via Playwright).
Contextual Sizing Presentation vs. Documentation Dynamic typography (e.g., 16px labels for 16:9 slides, 12px for inline docs).
Density Level Faithful, Balanced, Simplified Caps node complexity (24 max for Faithful, 12 for Balanced, 7 for Simplified).
Audience Vocabulary Technical vs. Executive Adjusts nomenclature and terminology without changing the underlying architecture.

Pruning Logic: When simplifying dense diagrams, the tool follows a deterministic hierarchy: it strips decorative elements first, merges duplicates next, trims leaf clusters, and finally consolidates lower-level infrastructure nodes.

Automated Brand Harmony and Contrast Validation

One of the standout features of Diagram-design is its ability to match your existing brand identity:

  1. Website Palette Extraction: Provide a target URL, and the tool extracts background shades, text colors, button accents, and font stacks directly from the stylesheet.
  2. WCAG AA Compliance: Before finalizing the design, it verifies color contrast against WCAG AA standards. If small typography (9px–12px) fails accessibility checks, it calculates an adjusted accessible hex value with an explanatory diff.
  3. Persistent Project Styling: Once approved, your custom design tokens are saved into the project’s style guide for all subsequent diagrams.

Installation & Local Workflow

Diagram-design runs completely local and is released under the MIT license:

# Example execution with npx / Codex / Claude Code skill setup
npx diagram-design init

Because Mermaid diagrams and vector primitives are parsed directly from text, no external network calls or telemetry are required. For exporting raster images (.png), ensure you have Playwright installed in your environment.

Whether you need an executive summary slide or detailed documentation for a system refactor, Diagram-design bridges the gap between raw ASCII specifications and publication-quality technical illustrations.

item.author: brzulovic@gmail.com
item.description:

While proprietary frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI have traditionally dominated developer workflows, modern open-weight architectures paired with specialized execution harnesses are flipping the script on raw model capability.

In this breakdown, James Layne demonstrates how configuring Qwen3.8 27B within a customized DeepSeek harness delivers superior task completion rates, lower latency, and dramatically reduced token costs compared to flagship proprietary alternatives within the Claude Code developer CLI.
item.content:encoded:
The landscape of autonomous coding agents is shifting at an unprecedented pace. While proprietary frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI have traditionally dominated developer workflows, modern open-weight architectures paired with specialized execution harnesses are flipping the script on raw model capability.

In this breakdown, James Layne demonstrates how configuring Qwen3.8 27B within a customized DeepSeek harness delivers superior task completion rates, lower latency, and dramatically reduced token costs compared to flagship proprietary alternatives within the Claude Code developer CLI.

Executive Summary & Key Takeaways

  • Scaffolding Multiplies Capability: Raw parameter size is no longer the sole determinant of coding performance. A well-engineered harness structure combined with recursive verification loops enables smaller models like Qwen 27B to out-resolve frontier giants.
  • Unmatched Cost-to-Performance: Running a quantized or locally hosted 27B parameter model drastically reduces API token expenditure without sacrificing code quality.
  • Claude Code Extensibility: By redirecting provider endpoints and standardizing tool calling schemas, developers can slot open-weight models directly into modern agentic CLI tools.
  • Deterministic Grounding: DeepSeek’s test-harness evaluation framework grounds code changes through real-time feedback loops, preventing the conversational hallucination traps often seen in large frontier models.

Key Timestamps & Video Breakdown

  • [00:00] - Overview & Architectural Thesis: Introduction to the performance parity gap between open models and Claude Opus.
  • [02:15] - The DeepSeek Harness Architecture: How recursive reflection and execution feedback empower mid-sized parameter models.
  • [05:40] - Setting Up Qwen3.8 27B Locally & Remotely: Configuration options using vLLM and Ollama alongside Claude Code.
  • [08:50] - Live Benchmark Suite: Running complex refactor tasks, dependency conflict resolutions, and automated test migrations.
  • [12:30] - Claude Code Integration Guide: Step-by-step custom proxy routing and tool declaration mapping.
  • [15:10] - Cost and Accuracy Analysis: Breakdown of token throughput, cost efficiency, and final verdict.

Detailed Topic Deep-Dive: Agent Harness Scaffolding

The Architecture Behind the Leap

When frontier models fail on multi-file code refactoring, failure is rarely caused by syntax ignorance; it stems from context drift and brittle tool execution. DeepSeek’s harness patterns enforce a rigorous three-tier execution loop:

  1. Planning & Context Pruning: Identifying the minimum necessary AST slice before generating diffs.
  2. Targeted Code Generation: Qwen3.8 produces clean, unified diffs formatted strictly for programmatic patch applications.
  3. Automated Verification: The harness runs local test suites and linters, feeding failures back into the prompt window before marking tasks as complete.
Attribute Vanilla Frontier Model Qwen3.8 27B + DeepSeek Harness
Model Size Massive Closed MoE 27B Open-Weights
Execution Pattern Linear Chain-of-Thought Cyclic Scaffolding & Verification
Cost per 1M Tokens ~$15.00 - $75.00 Local ($0.00) or ~$0.20 API
Context Drift Resistance Moderate High (Isolated Context Buffers)

Step-by-Step Configuration & Implementation

To route Claude Code or similar terminal agent CLIs to a custom Qwen3.8 27B endpoint wrapped in an agentic harness, you can proxy the API calls through an OpenAI-compatible interface using vLLM:

# Launch Qwen3.8 27B with high-throughput vLLM backend
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --port 8000

Next, configure your environment variables to point Claude Code toward the local harness bridge:

# Redirect Claude Code endpoint to local agent proxy
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8000/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="custom-local-key"

# Run Claude Code CLI
claude

// Example: Custom Tool Schema for DeepSeek Scaffolding Verification
interface HarnessToolCall {
  tool_name: "execute_bash_command" | "apply_diff";
  parameters: {
    command?: string;
    patch?: string;
    target_file?: string;
  };
  feedback_loop: boolean;
}

Key Quotes & Insights from James Layne

“The biggest revelation of this benchmark is that a 27-billion parameter model with strict verification loops routinely catches subtle regressions that massive 1-trillion parameter closed models glide right past.”

“Developers often default to closed APIs assuming higher cost equals higher intelligence. In software engineering tasks, deterministic tooling and grounded feedback beat parameter count every day of the week.”

Conclusion & Next Steps

Combining lean, highly capable open-weight models like Qwen3.8 27B with robust execution scaffolding represents the future of autonomous development environments. By reclaiming ownership of the model pipeline, engineering teams gain privacy, cut operating costs, and achieve faster execution loops.

To replicate these benchmarks, review the official Qwen documentation and integrate custom endpoint proxies into your favorite CLI agent tools today.

item.content:encoded:
Overview

OpenFox is an autonomous coding agent built specifically for local LLMs, designed to provide a comprehensive development environment right out of the box. By leveraging a contract-driven execution pipeline, it ensures that your code meets specific acceptance criteria, creating a reliable loop for automated software development.

Quick Start

Getting started with OpenFox is straightforward. Ensure you have Node.js (>= 24.0.0) installed, then install the package globally:

npm i -g openfox
openfox

On the first run, OpenFox will automatically detect your local LLM backend—supporting vLLM, sglang, ollama, and llamacpp—and configure itself accordingly.

Key Features of Version 2.0

The 2.0 release brings significant improvements to the agentic workflow:

  • Multi-Turn Agent Engine: A completely rewritten agent loop that utilizes EventStore as a single source of truth, unifying all modes like planning, building, and verifying.
  • Provider Dialog: A comprehensive UI for configuring providers, including reasoning efforts and profile management.
  • Unified Image Handling: Automatic vision model fallback allows any model to process images by generating descriptions before each turn.
  • Safe File Editing: A per-file mutex system prevents race conditions during parallel edits.
  • Enhanced Workflows: Support for workflow sub-groups and a dedicated code review phase.

CLI Commands & Options

You can manage your development environment directly from the terminal:

Option Description Default
-p, --port <number> Specify server port 10369
--no-browser Don’t open browser on start Opens browser
-h, --help Show help message -
-v, --version Show version number -

Common commands include:

# Start server for current project
openfox

# Manage LLM providers
openfox provider add
openfox provider list

# Show current configuration
openfox config

Extensibility via Plugins

OpenFox allows for modular functionality via plugins. You can add support for various services by installing plugins in your configuration directory:

  • ChatGPT Plus/Pro: openfox-chatgpt
  • Github Copilot: openfox-github-copilot
  • Google Antigravity: openfox-google-antigravity
  • xAI SuperGrok: openfox-xai-supergrok

Environment Configuration

OpenFox provides granular control through environment variables. Key variables include:

  • OPENFOX_LLM_URL: Set the API base URL (default: http://localhost:8000/v1).
  • OPENFOX_MAX_CONTEXT: Defines the maximum context window (default: 200000).
  • OPENFOX_DB_PATH: The path to the SQLite database used for session storage.

Note: Always ensure your backend LLM is compatible with the OpenAI API format to ensure full integration with OpenFox’s features.

item.content:encoded:
Modern AI coding assistants often lock developers into cloud ecosystems and proprietary subscriptions. OpenFox flips the script by providing a local-LLM-first, autonomous coding agent that comes fully configured straight out of the box.

With contract-driven execution pipelines, native support for popular local inference backends, and multi-turn workflows, OpenFox gives you complete control over your AI-assisted development stack without sacrificing agentic power.

Key Architectural Highlights

OpenFox combines structured planning, rigorous criteria verification, and local execution:

  • Contract-Driven Execution: Uses acceptance criteria as an immutable contract between you and the agent.
  • Plan → Builder Pipeline: Interactive task decomposition followed by autonomous code generation.
  • Iterative Verification: Loops and executes unit tests, builds, and checks until all defined criteria pass.
  • Language Server Protocol (LSP) Support: Built-in LSP communication gives the agent immediate feedback on compile and type errors.
  • Real-Time Performance Metrics: Transparent tracking of prefill time, token generation rate, and total context window utilization.

Quick Start

Getting started with OpenFox requires Node.js (>= 24.0.0) and an OpenAI-compatible local model server running locally (e.g., vLLM, sglang, Ollama, or llama.cpp).

Install the package globally via npm:

npm i -g openfox
openfox

On the initial launch, OpenFox automatically probes and detects active local inference endpoints, configuring the connection parameters without manual intervention.

What’s New in OpenFox 2.0

The 2.0 release brings major performance, stability, and extensibility improvements to the agent lifecycle:

1. Unified Multi-Turn Agent Engine

The agent loop has been redesigned from the ground up using an event-sourced EventStore architecture. All modes—planner, builder, verifier, and sub-agents—execute through the exact same unified loop.

2. Enhanced Provider Configuration

A brand-new Provider Dialog introduces UI-level controls for reasoning effort (reasoningEffort), profile defaults, and provider presets.

3. Configurable Auto-Retry Logic

Replaces rigid XML safeguards with custom regex and pattern-matching triggers that tell the model when to retry tool generation.

4. Cross-Model Vision Fallback

For setups running text-only LLMs alongside vision tasks, OpenFox introduces automatic pre-turn visual descriptions so any model can understand uploaded images.

5. Unified Session Metadata & Sub-Groups

A centralized session_metadata tool enables granular CRUD operations on criteria directly inside the UI. Additionally, workflow sub-groups allow isolating specific phases like automated code review.

6. Concurrency Safety

A per-file mutex locks concurrent edit_file calls, preventing race conditions during parallel file modifications.

CLI Reference

OpenFox includes a dedicated CLI for server management and provider administration.

Common Commands

# Start the OpenFox server in the current workspace
openfox

# Run on a custom port
openfox --port 8080

# Start in headless mode (suppress browser launch)
openfox --no-browser

# Inspect current setup
openfox config

# Provider management
openfox provider add
openfox provider list
openfox provider use
openfox provider remove

CLI Options

Option Description Default
-p, --port <number> Specify web server port 10369
--no-browser Prevent automatic browser launch Opens browser
-h, --help Display help menu —
-v, --version Display installed version —

Extending OpenFox with Plugins

OpenFox supports a plugin system to inject extra authentication providers, transport protocols, and model discovery without touching core code.

Plugin Directories by OS

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/openfox/plugins
  • Linux: ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/openfox/plugins
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\openfox\plugins

Supported Provider Plugins

  • openfox-chatgpt: Connect directly using ChatGPT Plus/Pro credentials.
  • openfox-github-copilot: Authenticate using GitHub Copilot.
  • openfox-google-antigravity: Google Cloud and Antigravity endpoint support.
  • openfox-xai-supergrok: xAI Grok provider connector.

Configuration & Environment Variables

You can customize your instance using environment variables:

Variable Default Description
OPENFOX_LLM_URL http://localhost:8000/v1 Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible local LLM endpoint
OPENFOX_BACKEND unknown Active backend engine (vllm, sglang, ollama, llamacpp)
OPENFOX_MAX_CONTEXT 200000 Context window ceiling in tokens
OPENFOX_PORT 10369 OpenFox local web server port
OPENFOX_HOST 127.0.0.1 Local listening host
OPENFOX_REASONING_EFFORT none Extended reasoning depth (none, low, medium, high)
OPENFOX_LOG_LEVEL info Logging verbosity (debug, info, warn, error)
OPENFOX_DB_PATH ./openfox.db Embedded SQLite database location

Conclusion

OpenFox represents a significant step forward for developers seeking a self-hosted, private, and agentic coding assistant. By combining strict contract-driven task verification with support for the latest open-weight models, it unlocks enterprise-grade AI pairing directly on local hardware.
